title: INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE

spans.text: “INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE” is a tool for solving a concrete programming problem. Identify the input and desired result, then trace what role the construct plays in the example. Study it not only as syntax, but also for its effects on readability, correctness, resource use, and future changes.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.
INSERT adds a row, UPDATE changes the matching row, and DELETE removes it.

DML changes table data. INSERT adds rows, UPDATE changes matching rows, and DELETE removes matching rows. Preview the same WHERE condition with SELECT before changing data, and use a transaction when several writes must act as one unit.

Key line: `INSERT INTO products (product_id, name, price_cents)`
What it does: INSERT adds a row, UPDATE changes the matching row, and DELETE removes it.
Why it is used: Preview the target rows with SELECT before UPDATE or DELETE, and understand the backup policy first.
If omitted or changed: Naming INSERT columns makes the statement resilient to later schema changes.

spans.title: Common mistake
spans.text: Forgetting WHERE in UPDATE or DELETE can change or remove every row.
